channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Israeli Intelligence Warns of Potential Iranian Assassination Attempt on Trump
item.description: Israeli intelligence has reportedly warned of a potential Iranian assassination attempt against Donald Trump. Following this warning, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Pentagon chief Pete Hegset have allegedly been moved to protected facilities, and Trump's public appearances are restricted.

item.title: Taliban Finance Minister Meets with Iranian Foreign Minister
item.description: The Taliban's Finance Minister held a meeting with the Iranian Foreign Minister. The details of their discussions were not immediately available. This meeting signifies ongoing diplomatic engagement between the Taliban administration and neighboring countries.

item.title: Afghanistan's absence from ECO foreign ministers' meeting raises questions
item.description: Afghanistan's absence from the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) foreign ministers' meeting in Islamabad has raised questions. Despite its ECO membership and strategic location, the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan did not participate. Member states are discussing economic cooperation, trade, and connectivity. Analysts warn that excluding Afghanistan could undermine ECO's objectives.

item.title: Uzbekistan Temporarily Halts Phone IMEI Registration Amid Smuggling Schemes
item.description: Uzbekistan's Customs Committee temporarily suspended phone IMEI registration at Tashkent airport due to schemes circumventing duty-free limits. The issue was resolved within a day. The committee also stated that phone import duties will be eliminated upon WTO accession, though VAT will remain. Official phone imports reached 4.1 million units in the first 10 months.

item.title: ASEAN Maintains Restrictions on Myanmar's Military Authorities
item.description: ASEAN leaders decided to adhere to their existing five-point peace plan regarding Myanmar at the Manila summit. Despite proposals to change the approach, no easing of restrictions against the country's military authorities was implemented. The plan includes cessation of violence, dialogue, ASEAN mediation, and humanitarian aid.

item.title: Uzbekistan Recovers Over 832 Billion Soums in Delayed Wages
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Labor Inspectorate recovered over 832 billion soums in delayed wages for nearly 35,000 employees during January-September. The Ministry of Poverty Reduction and Employment reported that over 15,000 inspections identified more than 36,000 labor law violations, with education, construction, industry, and agriculture sectors most affected.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Prohibit Privatization of Land in Educational and Medical Institutions
item.description: Uzbekistan will prohibit the privatization of land located within educational and medical institutions, according to a presidential decree. A draft law is being prepared to implement this measure. Efforts will also be made to increase green spaces in district and city centers to 30%.

item.title: Almaty Shuts Off Water Supply to Non-Compliant Car Washes
item.description: Almaty authorities have disconnected water supply to several car washes for violating operational rules. Investigations revealed that seven car washes lacked essential water recycling systems. These facilities can have their water supply restored only after installing the required equipment and passing inspection.

item.title: Man Dies by Suicide in Helmand Due to Economic Hardship and Unemployment
item.description: A 30-year-old man in Helmand Province died by suicide due to poverty and economic hardship. Identified as Ahmad Wali, he had been unemployed for a long time and was reportedly struggling with financial difficulties and debt. This incident highlights the growing economic challenges in Afghanistan.

item.title: Tashkent Reports 307 New HIV Cases in Nine Months; Sexual Transmission Dominant
item.description: Tashkent has recorded 307 new HIV cases in the first nine months of the year. A significant majority, 75.9%, of these new infections are attributed to sexual transmission. The city has also seen an increase in individuals registered for mental health and addiction services.

item.title: Taliban Detain Two Community Representatives in Kabul's Omid-e Sabz Township
item.description: Two community representatives in Kabul's Omid-e Sabz Township have been detained by the Taliban's Ministry of Justice for nearly a week. Other representatives were released after agreeing to vacate the area. Families have no information on the detainees' condition or whereabouts amid claims that the Taliban declared the land state property.

item.title: Kazakhstan Transport Minister Reverses Stroller Ban on Public Buses
item.description: Kazakhstan's Transport Minister Assel Zhanasova has decided to review regulations regarding the transport of baby strollers on public buses, aiming to eliminate ambiguous interpretations. The minister emphasized the importance of public transport being convenient and accessible for families with young children, ensuring no parent is forced to leave a bus due to stroller issues.

item.title: New Section of Aktobe-Kandyagash Highway in Kazakhstan Becomes Toll Road
item.description: An 89-kilometer section of the Aktobe-Kandyagash highway, a road of republican significance in Kazakhstan's Aktobe region, has been integrated into the existing Kandyagash-Makat toll road system. The new charges, effective November 15, apply to all vehicle types on a specific segment, with discounts available for local residents and annual passes offered.

item.title: Kremlin's Conditions for Ending War Revealed by Media Reports
item.description: Media reports have revealed the terms under which the Kremlin is prepared to end the war. These new demands reportedly echo Russia's ultimatum to Europe and NATO in late 2021, prior to the full-scale invasion, and are said to apply not only to the EU and NATO but also to Moldova, Finland, and Central Asian countries.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to visit Oman for state talks
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to Oman, with high-level bilateral negotiations and meetings with major company leaders scheduled in Muscat on November 16-17.

item.title: Taliban forces detain two female health workers in Bamiyan for traveling without guardians
item.description: Taliban forces detained two female health workers in Afghanistan's Bamiyan province for traveling without male guardians. Sources reported they were held for 24 hours, subjected to verbal abuse, and released.

item.title: Taliban intelligence arrests private university lecturer Din Mohammad Jawid in Kabul
item.description: Taliban intelligence agents have arrested Din Mohammad Jawid, a lecturer at a private university and writer, at his home in Kabul. His whereabouts are currently unknown, and the reasons for his arrest remain unclear.

item.title: Taliban Suspend Classes at Kabul University for Mullahs' Gathering
item.description: Sources report that Kabul University has been closed by the Taliban for one week to host a gathering of approximately 4,000 mullahs. The event aims to express support for decrees issued by the group's leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. Educational activities for all students are suspended until November 19.

item.title: Kabul Hospital Closed by Justice Minister's Order, Owner Claims
item.description: Jawad Mohseni, owner of Khatam al-Nabieen Hospital, states the facility was shut down by Kabul authorities on the Justice Minister's orders after he refused to hand over management. The hospital provided services for over 15 years, particularly in kidney treatment and urology.

item.title: Uzbek President to Visit Oman on State Visit November 16-17
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to Oman from November 16-17 at the invitation of Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said. The agenda includes high-level bilateral talks in Muscat, meetings with business leaders, and discussions on expanding cooperation in trade, investment, and agriculture.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports 1.4 Million Citizens Living in Poverty
item.description: As of October 1, 1.4 million people in Uzbekistan are classified as poor, according to the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction. This represents 3.6% of the population, down from 5.8% at the start of the year when 2.2 million citizens were identified as poor. The ministry focuses on targeted support for each family.

item.title: Turkey Detains 35 Afghan Migrants Attempting to Reach Greece by Sea
item.description: Turkish police apprehended 35 Afghan migrants attempting to cross into Greece by sea in Balikesir province. Four suspects accused of migrant smuggling were also arrested. Police seized life jackets and pumps. The migrants were transferred to a reception center, and three of the four suspects were remanded in custody.

item.title: UK Envoy to Visit Pakistan for Afghanistan-Related Dialogue
item.description: The UK's Special Representative for Afghanistan, Richard Lindsay, will visit Pakistan to discuss regional developments and facilitate dialogue on issues between Afghanistan and Pakistan. He met virtually with Mullah Abdul Wasi, Chief of Staff of the IEA Prime Minister's Office, who thanked the UK for its humanitarian aid and efforts to resolve bilateral issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Unified 'One Stop' Customs Control with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan is in negotiations with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan to implement a unified 'One Stop' customs control system at select border crossings. Three potential models are being considered: joint operations in one building, separate agency operations with clear responsibilities, or mutual recognition of customs procedures and data exchange. The initiative's launch timeline is not yet determined.

item.title: Expert Recalls Data on Kazakhstan's Territory Transfer to Uzbekistan in 1956
item.description: Expert Eldar Konayev highlighted that in 1956, a portion of Kazakhstan's territory, including the Bostandyk district, was transferred to Uzbekistan. He noted that politician Zhumabek Tashenov led the initiative group that proposed this transfer.

item.title: Appeals Court in Tashkent Replaces Suspended Sentences with Real Prison Terms for Blogger Kokow and Actress Barchin Gafurova
item.description: An appellate court in Tashkent has replaced suspended sentences with real prison terms for blogger Kokow, actress Barchin Gafurova, and a third woman. They were found guilty of extortion and insult, receiving sentences ranging from 3.5 to 4.5 years.

item.title: Almaty to Ban Coal Heating in Some Districts Starting 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Almaty will prohibit the use of coal, fuel, and oil for heating private homes in certain districts with low emission levels. This regulation, part of the Atmospheric Air Protection Rules adopted in 2025, applies to heating boilers and individual boilers for multi-story buildings. The affected area is currently defined by specific streets and is planned for expansion.

item.title: France Agrees to Receive Taliban Diplomats for Migration Talks
item.description: France has agreed to host Taliban diplomats for discussions on Afghan migrant returns, a source confirmed. French officials state these talks do not signify diplomatic recognition of the Taliban regime. The discussions aim to facilitate the return of Afghan nationals in France deemed security threats.

item.title: Senior Hamas Commander Killed in Israeli Strikes on Gaza
item.description: A senior commander of Hamas has been killed in Israeli airstrikes targeting the Gaza Strip. The incident marks a significant escalation in the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas.

item.title: IOM Records Over 95,000 Border Movements Into Afghanistan in Two Weeks
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded 95,489 movements into Afghanistan between October 25 and November 7. The majority, 68%, were from Iran, and 32% from Pakistan. During the same period, 44,899 movements out of Afghanistan were recorded, primarily towards Iran and Pakistan.

item.title: Chronic Sleep Deprivation Increases Risk of Heart Attack and Stroke, Doctor Warns
item.description: According to somnologist Ilya Smirnov, consistently insufficient sleep accelerates atherosclerosis, significantly raising the risk of vascular diseases like heart attack and stroke. He highlighted obstructive sleep apnea as particularly dangerous, especially when combined with excess weight, leading to oxygen deprivation and stress hormone release.

item.title: NATO Cancels Planned 2027 Leaders Summit in Albania, Reduces Ministerial Meetings
item.description: NATO has decided not to hold its planned leaders' summit in Albania in 2027, though a summit in 2028 is not ruled out. The alliance is also reducing the number of defense and foreign affairs ministerial meetings. NATO states summits are held when necessary, not annually.

item.title: Bahrain Issues Security Warnings Amid Escalating Iran-US Tensions in Gulf
item.description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued security warnings, urging residents to seek safety amid rising tensions between Iran and the United States in the Gulf. The alerts, posted on X, followed claims by Iran's IRGC of targeting a US radar installation. Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters.

item.title: UK Special Envoy Discusses Easing Taliban-Pakistan Tensions
item.description: UK Special Representative for Afghanistan Richard Lindsay is engaging in talks to ease tensions and normalize relations between the Taliban and Pakistan. Lindsay plans to visit Pakistan for further discussions with officials. The Taliban expressed appreciation for UK's humanitarian aid and efforts towards regional peace.

item.title: Israeli intelligence: Iran plans assassination attempt on Trump
item.description: Israeli intelligence agency Mossad has reportedly shared information with the CIA indicating Iran may be planning an assassination attempt on U.S. President Donald Trump and other high-ranking American officials. The report, citing sources, suggests Iran might use attack drones as part of the plot. This follows previous warnings and skepticism from U.S. intelligence.

item.title: Central Asian Fathers Embrace Active Roles Beyond Traditional Breadwinning
item.description: Fathers in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan are increasingly involved in their children's daily lives, moving beyond the traditional role of sole provider. Stories highlight fathers reading, helping with homework, and discussing feelings, fostering closer bonds.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Free Medications List Starting 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase the range of free medications provided to the public starting in 2027. An electronic policy will be introduced via the Single Interactive State Services portal, detailing each citizen's status, available free medical services, and medication list.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Orders Probe into Yandex Service Failures and Data Leaks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General has ordered a comprehensive review of the Information Security Committee's activities and an investigation into failures within Yandex services. This action follows concerns about the public disclosure of Kazakh citizens' personal data. The probe aims to ensure compliance with constitutional rights protecting personal data.

item.title: Yemeni Government Seeks International Aid to Recapture Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Houthis
item.description: The official Yemeni government has appealed to the international community for assistance in retaking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Houthi control. This strategic waterway is crucial for global shipping and has been a point of contention in the ongoing conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan and ACWA to Explore Carbon Credit Generation at Wind Farms
item.description: Uzbekistan and ACWA have signed a memorandum of cooperation on carbon markets and international greenhouse gas reduction mechanisms. The agreement focuses on exploring the inclusion of ACWA's wind power projects in Uzbekistan into international carbon market mechanisms under the Paris Agreement, including carbon credit generation.
